## Description
Read a binary sequence from standard input and report whether there exists a single uppercase English string of the same length whose permitted operations can turn every entry into a 1.

## Preconditions
- **PRE-1 (Unverified):** The first input line contains an integer \(N\), with \(3 \le N \le 200{,}000\).
- **PRE-2 (Unverified):** The second input line contains exactly \(N\) integers, each either 0 or 1.

## Postconditions
- **POST-1 (Unverified):** Standard output contains one verdict: `Yes` if at least one good string exists, or `No` otherwise. Letter case does not matter.
- **POST-2 (Unverified):** For the verdict, a candidate is good exactly when it is a fixed string of \(N\) uppercase English letters and a finite sequence of permitted operations, possibly empty, leaves no zeros. At any starting position, a consecutive `ARC` or `CRA` in the candidate permits setting the two sequence entries at the first and second positions of that triple to 1. Both the string and sequence wrap from position \(N\) to position 1.
- **POST-3 (Unverified):** Each permitted operation leaves the candidate string and all other sequence entries unchanged. It may set an entry that is already 1, and no operation changes a 1 to a 0. An input containing only ones therefore receives `Yes`.

## Test suggestions
- At the minimum length, check that `0 0 0` yields `No`, `0 0 1` yields `Yes`, and `1 1 1` yields `Yes` (PRE-1, PRE-2, POST-1–POST-3).
- At length 3, check that `0 1 0` yields `Yes`: the fixed candidate `RCA` permits an `ARC` operation starting at position 3, covering entries 3 and 1 (POST-1, POST-2).
- At the maximum length, check that an all-ones sequence yields `Yes` without requiring any operation (PRE-1, POST-3).

## Unspecified behavior
Malformed or out-of-range input is outside the guarantees. No witness string, operation sequence, or explanation is required, and no preference among valid witnesses or operation orders is specified.
